You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Step 2. Recalibrate the battery sensor software (10 minutes)
Step 3. Snap the internal plastic shroud back into place (30 seconds)

Step 56. Restart the device to verify power-on (2 minutes)
Step 57. Gather the necessary screwdrivers and spudgers (3 minutes)
Step 58. Remove any leftover adhesive residue (5 minutes)
Step 59. Check the replacement battery's manufacture date (1 minute)
Step 60. Open the toolbox and select the PH0 bit (30 seconds)
Step 61. Discharge the internal capacitors (5 minutes)
Step 62. Turn off the workbench lamp to check for sparks (30 seconds)
Step 63. Tuck the sensor wires into the side channel (1 minute)
Step 64. Identify the correct replacement part number (5 minutes)
Step 65. Set aside the external cover screws (1 minute)
Step 66. Unbox the new battery carefully (2 minutes)
Step 67. Re-apply the rubber foot pads (2 minutes)
Step 68. Secure the cable connector latch (15 seconds)
Step 69. Remove the external casing or back panel (5 minutes)
Step 70. Put on latex-free gloves (1 minute)
Step 71. Loosen the external case screws (3 minutes)
Step 72. Ground yourself to the chassis (10 seconds)
Step 73. Connect the new battery to the motherboard (30 seconds)
Step 74. Verify the system clock and time zone (2 minutes)
Step 75. Peel back the protective tape over the connector (30 seconds)
Step 76. Apply a drop of thread locker to the bracket screw (30 seconds)
Step 77. Lift the battery connector using a plastic tool (30 seconds)
Step 78. Reassemble the internal frame (6 minutes)
Step 79. Disconnect the CMOS battery if required (1 minute)
Step 80. Wipe the exterior of the device (2 minutes)
Step 81. Test the power button for tactile response (10 seconds)
Step 82. Apply a thin layer of thermal paste if needed (2 minutes)
Step 83. Confirm the battery capacity in the BIOS (4 minutes)
Step 84. Inspect the old battery for physical damage (1 minute)
Step 85. Check the workspace lighting (1 minute)
Step 86. Tighten the battery bracket screws (45 seconds)
Step 87. Compare the old and new battery dimensions (2 minutes)
Step 88. Document the battery's cycle count (2 minutes)
Step 89. Remove the laptop's bottom cover (4 minutes)
Step 90. Clear any debris from the battery connector (1 minute)
Step 91. Take a final photo of the finished assembly (1 minute)
Step 92. Read the troubleshooting guide for power issues (10 minutes)
Step 93. Place the device on a soft anti-static mat (1 minute)
Step 94. Check for any bulging in the device chassis (2 minutes)
Step 95. Verify you have the correct screwdriver bits (2 minutes)
Step 96. Use a plastic spudger to release the clips (3 minutes)
Step 97. Check that the casing is flush on all sides (1 minute)
Step 98. Press down on the battery to seat it firmly (15 seconds)
Step 99. Locate the battery compartment door (30 seconds)
Step 100. Inspect the new battery's connector pins (1 minute)
